questions.q: Why is a standing privileged account a significant security risk, according to this lesson?
options: It carries no more risk than any ordinary user account
It is only risky if the password is written down on paper
It is a maximum-value target that is already privileged the instant it's compromised, exposed continuously even when the privilege isn't being used
It is risky only during the first week after the account is created
questions.explain: A standing admin account never needs to wait for the right moment — it's immediately useful to an attacker the moment it's compromised.

options: Storing privileged account passwords in an encrypted vault, checked out on demand instead of memorized or shared
A method for encrypting all user passwords, privileged or not, the same way
Writing privileged passwords down and locking them in a physical safe
A technique for guessing privileged account passwords during a penetration test
questions.explain: Vaulting means nobody memorizes the privileged credential — it's checked out from the vault under a logged, attributable event.

questions.q: What does session recording add on top of credential vaulting?
options: A faster way to check out credentials from the vault
The ability to skip multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts
Automatic password rotation after every login
Visibility into what actually happened during a privileged session, not just who obtained the credential
questions.explain: Vaulting controls who can obtain privileged credentials; session recording captures what was actually done once they were used.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, named example of a PAM tool or platform mentioned in this lesson?
options: A standard firewall appliance
CyberArk and Azure PIM (Privileged Identity Management)
A generic antivirus suite
Microsoft Word and Excel
questions.explain: CyberArk is a long-standing dedicated PAM platform; Azure PIM is Microsoft Entra ID's cloud-native privileged access tool.

questions.q: Why does rotating a privileged credential's password after checkout matter?
options: It prevents the same credential from being reused without going through the vault again
It is required only for cloud accounts, never for on-premises systems
It makes the password easier for administrators to memorize
It removes the need for any logging of who checked out the credential
questions.explain: Automatic rotation after use means a credential can't be reused outside the vault's logged, controlled checkout process.
